title: Preregistered claim-core amendment: IPM baseline equilibration recorded per attempt (QOCO native default), wall-clock deadline classification for uninterruptible solves, N=2000 hard bound recorded unchanged
frozen_before_any_group_result_inspected: Frozen while checkpoint build-integration-report/g4-claim-core-ccd5596 (amendment v1.1) held only pure-gpu-ipm groups; no group has run under this amendment. The v1.1 IPM records were inspected only to establish the rule-A probe evidence below and are quarantined as the diagnostic stratum ipm_no_equilibration_v1_1, never as H6 evidence.
record_field_scope: every raw attempt record emitted by the executor
unchanged: quality tiers, tolerances and matched-quality gates (benchmarks/g4_policy.json unchanged)
the twenty evaluation seeds and physical instance identities
two same-session warm-ups followed by seven measured attempts per group
group identities (g4-group-v1 content addresses) and the frozen solver_order rotation
one process, one CUDA context and one persistent workspace per group
bootstrap seed, sample count, confidence and decision thresholds
the claim core resolves H5 and H6 only and feeds no F01-F12/T01-T08 product
every v1.1 rule (run-and-flag contamination, deterministic replay, 120 s / 200k censoring, 10% censoring-sensitivity stratum) and the amended 396-group schedule identity
the campaign scaling_mode axis and its PDHCG meaning for adaptive, fixed-tight and the PDHCG stage of hybrid-pdhcg-ipm

ipm_equilibration.fairness_basis: docs/COMPARATIVE_SOLVER_CAMPAIGN.md: each system runs its native algorithm at documented default/best-feasible settings; matched final quality, not matched internals. The IPM baseline therefore ignores the PDHCG-oriented scaling_mode axis and uses QOCO's own equilibration setting.
ipm_equilibration.selection_rule: The executor hands QOCO settings.ruiz_iters = ruiz_iterations for every IPM solve (pure-gpu-ipm attempts and the IPM stage of hybrid-pdhcg-ipm) regardless of the coordinate scaling_mode; each raw attempt echoes amendment.ipm_equilibration {mode, ruiz_iterations, requested_ruiz_iterations, scaling_mode, qoco_status_code}. Non-IPM policies carry ipm_equilibration = null.

qoco_default_at_pinned_commit.note: The request assumed QOCO's default is 'Ruiz on'. At the pinned commit the shipped default is no Ruiz equilibration; 'native default' therefore means ruiz_iters = 0. Ruiz-on (5 iterations) was probed and is not selected: see probe_evidence.

probe_evidence.coordinate: P1-E-low-thrust N=100 claim-core group a8bdf61e (conditioning 4.0, the failing coordinate) and the same coordinate at conditioning 0.0; foreground, contaminated by a foreign Windows compute job, attempt deadline 120 s, cap 200000
probe_evidence.adaptive_conditioning_interpretation: 'one adaptive-conditioning coordinate' was read as the other level of the claim-core conditioning axis (0.0) for the same family/scale; hybrid-pdhcg-ipm at conditioning 4.0 was also probed.

probes.disposition: numerical (8/8; group hit the 1140 s group deadline, 1 unrun)
probes.qoco_status: numerical error (QOCO status 5) on every solve
probes.note: under rule B the 7 attempts with wall > 120 s become timeout

probes.note: the NaNs are a QOCO CUDA-backend Ruiz defect, not data scaling

probes.qoco_status: numerical error after 54 iterations, best iterate 9 restored, no NaN

probes.qoco_status: numerical error, best iterate 11-16 restored, no NaN
probes.note: Ruiz-on turns a converging coordinate into a failing one

probes.label: hybrid_cond4_ruiz5_and_ruiz0

probe_evidence.conclusion: QOCO native equilibration (Ruiz) does not rescue the failing P1-E N=100 conditioning-4.0 coordinate: with the pinned library it produces NaN iterates (QOCO defect); with the defects patched it still ends in numerical error and is slower; on the converging conditioning-0.0 coordinate it turns qualified solves into numerical failures. The conditioning-4.0 IPM result stands as a genuine IPM negative on this problem class. The amendment selects QOCO's actual pinned default (ruiz_iters = 0) as the native baseline and records it on every IPM attempt.

qoco_cuda_ruiz_defects.defect: safe_div(1.0, 0.0) returns QOCOFloat_MAX for a zero-infinity-norm row or column, so structurally empty rows of G/A (present in the SCvx formulation) receive a DBL_MAX scale and the scaled problem overflows to NaN
qoco_cuda_ruiz_defects.status_observed: numerical error (5) at iteration 8 with NaN residuals

qoco_cuda_ruiz_defects.defect: no host fallback: Ruiz runs on host data but scale_arrayf only launches a device kernel, so P and c are never scaled while the bookkeeping scale k is, collapsing the objective scale
qoco_cuda_ruiz_defects.status_observed: objective overflow / DBL_MAX cost with Ruiz > 0
qoco_cuda_ruiz_defects.scratch_fix: host-pointer loop when the array is not device memory

ipm_equilibration.not_papered_over: The NaNs were traced to the two defects above rather than to problem data. The pinned library is unchanged for the campaign; the scratch fixes were used only to separate 'Ruiz is broken in this build' from 'Ruiz does not help this problem class'.

deadline_classification.statement: An IPM (or any) solve may be uninterruptible. If a launched attempt's measured wall time exceeds the attempt deadline, the attempt is classified timeout with reason wall_exceeded_deadline; the completed solve's residuals, iteration counts and the solver's own disposition are attached as diagnostics (amendment.deadline_classification.solver_disposition). An executor_defect keeps its disposition.
deadline_classification.statistics: wall-clock timeouts are censoring, identical to a cooperative timeout

hard_bound.statement: N=2000 groups keep the single-gpu-v1 hard bound: an executor that exceeds the group deadline is killed, restarted exactly once (restart_generation 1), and a second breach produces an error record for the group.

ipm_no_equilibration_v1_1.reason: pure-gpu-ipm records taken under amendment v1.1 before rule A recorded the equilibration selection and before rule B existed; the executor was correct but the records are not comparable to v1.2 records

contamination.rule: A measured or warm-up attempt whose execution window overlaps any monitor sample reporting foreign GPU compute (a foreign WSL /dev/dxg holder with CUDA devices visible, or a host compute-only context with non-zero SM or memory utilization) is flagged contaminated=true. Its disposition and quality metrics are retained; its timing and energy are invalid for statistics.

detection.before_during_after: boundary samples before and after the group plus ~1 s probes during it
detection.wsl_limitation: WSL2 nvidia-smi cannot enumerate foreign PIDs; foreign host processes are read from Windows nvidia-smi.exe pmon (SM%/MEM% per PID)
detection.utilization_deltas: GPU utilization, memory and power are recorded at both boundaries and at every probe; the group record stores the before/during/after utilization delta
detection.lock_file_rule: the worker holds the shared advisory lock with a JSON payload (pid, campaign, group_id, started) for the whole group and records any foreign payload found in it

contamination.statistics: Contaminated measured attempts never enter a timing or energy statistic or a paired bootstrap; they remain in disposition and quality counts. Every H5/H6 coordinate row reports the pair count n actually used, the contaminated count per policy, and censoring, so a reduced sample is visible rather than imputed.

deterministic_replay.trigger: warm-up/0, warm-up/1 and measured/0 of one group each reach the attempt deadline (disposition timeout, actually launched) with identical trace hashes
deterministic_replay.action: measured/1..6 are recorded unlaunched with disposition timeout_deterministic_replay, replay_source_attempt_id = <group>/measured-0, the source trace and zero wall time; they are not executed
deterministic_replay.fallback: if any of the three traces differ, all seven measured attempts are executed
deterministic_replay.statistics: replayed attempts count as timeout censoring; they never enter a timing statistic

censoring.scope: claim core only; the full G4 ledger keeps the original values
censoring.inner_iteration_cap_rule: every inner PDHCG iteration limit of the policy (fixed-tight limit, adaptive polish limit, final polish limit) becomes min(limit, cap); limits already below the cap are unchanged
censoring.group_deadline_rule: 9 x attempt deadline + 60 s, as in single-gpu-v1

sensitivity_stratum.name: censoring_sensitivity
sensitivity_stratum.selection: sha256(selection_seed + '|' + group_id), lowest two per stratum
sensitivity_stratum.twin_identity: same coordinate plus censoring_stratum=censoring_sensitivity (distinct g4-group-v1 id, same physical instance)

censoring.acceptance_rule: For every sensitivity twin, each measured attempt (seed, repeat) is compared with the same attempt of its claim-core group. If any attempt is qualified under 600 s / 1M while its 120 s / 200k counterpart is timeout or timeout_deterministic_replay (or the counterpart is missing while the twin qualified), the amendment is invalid: no H5/H6 decision is issued from the 120 s core and the full core reverts to 600 s / 1M.

schedule.rule: claim-core groups run in policy_priority order and, within a policy, in the claim core's definition order; each sensitivity twin runs immediately after its claim-core group
schedule.solver_order_note: The claim core never bound its execution order to the solver_order rotation (its scheduler ran definition order); solver_order stays recorded per group as an execution-only identity axis, so reordering is permitted.
